skill.name: bioservices
skill.description: Primary Python tool for 40+ bioinformatics services. Preferred for multi-database workflows: UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, PubChem, Reactome, QuickGO. Unified API for queries, ID mapping, pathway analysis. For direct REST control, use individual database skills.
skill.summary: Use BioServices to query biological databases, map identifiers, and build multi-service bioinformatics workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, biological identifier names, and documentation text. I confirmed the executable scripts that write to CLI-supplied paths because they can create or overwrite files if run with unsafe arguments. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve output paths under a chosen project directory or require confirmation before writing outside that directory.
Check for existing output files and prompt before overwriting generated CSV, SIF, or text reports.
Warn users before submitting private sequences, compounds, identifiers, or email addresses to external databases.
Clarify that shell commands are optional user actions and should be reviewed before execution.

content.value_statement: Bioinformatics work often requires queries across many biological databases. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through BioServices workflows for proteins, pathways, compounds, and identifier mapping.
actual_capabilities: Explains BioServices setup and usage for UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, PubChem, Reactome, QuickGO, and related services.
Provides workflows for protein search, FASTA retrieval, BLAST submission, pathway discovery, and GO annotation.
Includes scripts for protein analysis, pathway network export, compound cross-reference reports, and batch identifier conversion.
Documents identifier mapping between UniProt, KEGG, Ensembl, PDB, RefSeq, ChEBI, ChEMBL, PubChem, and DrugBank.
Shows output handling patterns for TSV, FASTA, dictionary responses, CSV files, and SIF interaction files.
limitations: Many workflows call external bioinformatics services and require internet access.
BLAST workflows may require an email address and can take several minutes.
Database availability, identifiers, and result formats can change outside the skill.
Scripts write output files and should be run only in a chosen workspace directory.

use_cases.title: Review Protein Function
use_cases.description: Find a protein entry, retrieve its sequence, map it to KEGG pathways, and collect Gene Ontology annotations.

use_cases.title: Map Compound Identifiers
use_cases.description: Search a compound name and cross-reference KEGG, ChEBI, ChEMBL, PubChem, and DrugBank identifiers.

use_cases.title: Export Pathway Networks
use_cases.description: Analyze organism pathways, summarize interaction counts, and export network files for downstream tools.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Protein Entry
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BioServices skill to identify the best UniProt entry for ZAP70_HUMAN. Summarize the accession, organism, sequence availability, and useful next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Identifier Lists
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BioServices batch identifier guidance to convert my UniProt accessions to KEGG identifiers. Explain how to handle unmapped identifiers and rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Reference a Compound
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a BioServices workflow for the compound Geldanamycin. Find KEGG, ChEBI, and ChEMBL identifiers and describe how to validate each match.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Service Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible BioServices pipeline for a protein target. Include UniProt search, FASTA retrieval, optional BLAST, KEGG pathway discovery, PSICQUIC interactions, QuickGO annotations, and output files.

output_examples.input: Identify ZAP70_HUMAN and suggest the next analysis steps.
output: The likely UniProt accession is P43403 for human ZAP70.
Next steps are FASTA retrieval, KEGG pathway mapping, GO annotation lookup, and optional BLAST similarity search.
Review the organism and accession before using the first search result in downstream work.
The workflow starts with a KEGG compound search by name.
It then extracts linked ChEBI data and maps the KEGG compound identifier to ChEMBL through UniChem.
The result is a concise report of matched identifiers and available compound properties.

output_examples.input: Analyze human KEGG pathways and export network data.
output: The pathway workflow collects human KEGG pathway identifiers and parses KGML pathway relations.
It summarizes pathway sizes, interaction counts, and relation types.
It can export summary tables, interaction files, and per-pathway details to a selected output directory.

best_practices: Confirm database identifiers and organism codes before running batch jobs.
Keep generated CSV, SIF, and text outputs in a dedicated project directory.
Use delays, limits, and retries to respect public service rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential sequences or unpublished compound data to public services without approval.
Do not run broad batch conversions without chunking and failure logging.
Do not assume the first search result is correct without checking organism and accession details.

faq.question: Does this skill call external services?
faq.answer: Yes. BioServices queries public databases such as UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, and QuickGO through their web APIs.

faq.question: Can it run BLAST searches?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an NCBI BLAST workflow, but BLAST can be slow and may require an email address.

faq.question: What input identifiers are supported?
faq.answer: It documents common UniProt, KEGG, GeneID, Ensembl, RefSeq, PDB, HGNC, GO, and compound identifiers.

faq.question: Does it create files?
faq.answer: The included scripts can write CSV, SIF, text, and failed-ID files in the selected output location.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for guided BioServices workflows.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for the official database APIs?
faq.answer: No. It helps use BioServices, but results and availability depend on the upstream databases.
